## Structural broad sectorGVA sector change 

```{r struct}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 16

# LOAD ITL3 GVA DATA----

#ITL3 zones, SIC sections, current prices, 2023 latest data (minus imputed rent)
df = read_csv('https://bit.ly/rtasteritl3noir')

#This one has imputed rent included if you want it
# df = read_csv('https://bit.ly/rtasteritl3')



#Finding location quotients for each year in the data 
#And then overwriting the df variable with the result
df = df %>%
  group_split(year) %>%
  map(add_location_quotient_and_proportions,
      regionvar = Region_name,
      lq_var = SIC07_description,
      valuevar = value) %>% 
  bind_rows()


#1. Set window for rolling average: 3 years
smoothband = 3

#2. Make new column with rolling average in (applying to all places and sectors)
#Years are already in the right order, so will roll apply across those correctly
df = df %>% 
  group_by(Region_name,SIC07_description) %>% 
  mutate(
    sector_regional_prop_movingav = rollapply(
      sector_regional_proportion,smoothband,mean,align='center',fill=NA
      )
  ) %>% 
  ungroup()


#Get set pastel colours for each SIC section
n <- length(unique(df$SIC07_description))
set.seed(12)
qual_col_pals = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal.info[RColorBrewer::brewer.pal.info$category == 'qual',]
col_vector = unlist(mapply(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal, qual_col_pals$maxcolors, rownames(qual_col_pals)))

randomcols <- col_vector[10:(10+(n-1))]

#Do once!
getplot <- function(place){
  
  df = df %>% 
    filter(!qg("Activities of households|agri",SIC07_description)) %>% 
    mutate(
      SIC07_description = reduceSICnames(names = SIC07_description, level = 'section')
    )
  
  top12sectors = df %>%
    filter(
      Region_name == place,
      year == max(year) - 1#to get 3 year moving average value
    ) %>%
    arrange(-sector_regional_prop_movingav) %>%
    slice_head(n= 12) %>%
    select(SIC07_description) %>%
    pull()
  
  
  ggplot(df %>% 
           filter(
             Region_name == place, 
             SIC07_description %in% top12sectors,
             !is.na(sector_regional_prop_movingav)#Remove NAs created by 3 year moving average
           ), 
         aes(x = year, y = sector_regional_prop_movingav * 100, colour = fct_reorder(SIC07_description,-sector_regional_prop_movingav) )) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_line() +
    scale_color_manual(values = setNames(randomcols,unique(df$SIC07_description))) +#set manual pastel colours matching sector name
    ylab('Sector: percent of regional economy') +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = 'bold')) +
    labs(colour = 'SIC section') +
    # scale_y_log10() +
    ggtitle(paste0(place, ' GVA % of economy over time\nTop 12 sectors in ',max(df$year),'\n (', smoothband,' year moving average)'))
  
  
}

places = getdistinct('bradford|kirklees|calderdale|leeds|wakefield',df$Region_name)

plots <- map(places, getplot)

patchwork::wrap_plots(plots, ncol = 1)


```




## GVA V JOBS


```{r gvajobs1}

#2015 to 2023, linked on the regional GVA bespoke SIC categories
#Note, can use lookup if need to also sum for sections (which we can do here cos current prices)
gvabres <- readRDS('data/regionalGVA_plus_BRESjobcounts/regionalGVA_currentprices_BRES_FT_jobcount_bespoke2digitSIC_nONLY_MATCHING_GEOGs_2015_2023.rds')

#Make abbreviated sector names
shortsectornames = tibble(
  SIC07_description = unique(gvabres$SIC07_description),
  SIC07_description_shortened = c(
  "Furniture",
  "Machinery",
  "Buildings",
  "Engineering",
  "Construction",
  "Motor",
  "Wholesale",
  "Retail",
  "Transport",
  "Warehousing",
  "Post",
  "Accommodation",
  "Food",
  "Media",
  "Telecoms",
  "RealEstate",
  "Legal",
  "Consultancy",
  "Architecture",
  "Research",
  "Professional",
  "Rental",
  "Employment",
  "Cleaning/landscapes",
  "Admin",
  "Health",
  "Care",
  "SocialWork",
  "Arts/ent",
  "Recreation",
  "Membership",
  "Repair",
  "Personal",
  "Agri/mining",
  "FoodManuf",
  "Textiles",
  "WoodPaper",
  "Chemicals",
  "Metals",
  "Electronics",
  "MachineryManuf",
  "Utilities",
  "Finance",
  "PublicAdmin",
  "Education",
  "Households"
  )
)

#save that for use elsewhere
write_csv(shortsectornames, 'data/shortsectornames_for_regionalGVA_2digitSICs.csv')

gvabres <- gvabres %>% 
  left_join(
    shortsectornames, by = 'SIC07_description'
  )



#For current prices - what we can do:
#Find GVA as a proportion of total UK output for those years
#Then that proportion per FT job
#To see how productivity has shifted about internally / how sectors have changed relative to each other

#That version is missing some places so isn't entire UK
#Let's get entire UK's GVA per year
#Can just sum from any current price source
#2023:
allgva <- read_csv('../data/regionalGVA/regionalGVA_currentprices_ITL2_SIC_2DIGIT_LONG_2023.csv')
#allgva <- read_csv('data/regionalGVA/regionalGVA_currentprices_ITL2_SIC_2DIGIT_LONG_2023.csv')




allgva <- allgva %>% 
  group_by(year) %>% 
  summarise(totalUKGVA_CP = sum(value)) %>% 
  ungroup()

#Add that in...
gvabres <- gvabres %>% 
  left_join(allgva, by = c('DATE'= 'year')
  )

#Some NAs in jobs - I think the issue with the missing values is just early years with no agri data...
#filter
gvabres <- gvabres %>% filter(!is.na(JOBCOUNT))


#Find gva proportion of UK total then the job's proportion of that
gvabres <- gvabres %>%
  mutate(
    gva_proportionofUKtotal = GVA / totalUKGVA_CP,
    job_output_propofUKtotal = gva_proportionofUKtotal / JOBCOUNT
  )




smoothband = 3

gvabres <- gvabres %>%
  group_by(Region_name,SIC07_description) %>%
  mutate(
    jobcount_movingav = rollapply(JOBCOUNT,smoothband,mean,align='center',fill=NA),
    gva_movingav = rollapply(GVA,smoothband,mean,align='center',fill=NA),
    job_output_propofUKtotal_movingav = rollapply(job_output_propofUKtotal,smoothband,mean,align='center',fill=NA)
  ) %>% 
  ungroup()



#ggplot won't give control over order very well... let's add on top manually, more control
prod.data <- gvabres %>% 
  mutate(
    DATE = DATE - 2000,#Make dates 2 digit, more readable on axis
    SIC07_description_shortened = fct_reorder(SIC07_description_shortened, job_output_propofUKtotal, .desc = T),
    highlow = ifelse(SIC07_description_shortened %in% levels(SIC07_description_shortened)[1:23],'high','low')#Break into two plots to stack, split by total av productivity
  ) %>% 
  filter(!qg('hous',SIC07_description), !is.na(job_output_propofUKtotal_movingav))
  


p1 <- ggplot() +
  geom_jitter(#Rest of UK first
    data =  prod.data %>% filter(highlow == 'high'),
    aes(x = DATE, y = job_output_propofUKtotal_movingav, group = Region_name),
    alpha = 0.3, size = 1, 
    width = 0.1) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0,0.0000005)) +
  geom_point(#Then Leeds and Bradford
    data =  prod.data %>% filter(Region_name %in% c('Leeds','Bradford'), highlow == 'high'),
    aes(x = DATE, y = job_output_propofUKtotal_movingav, group = Region_name, colour = Region_name, shape = Region_name),
    alpha = 1, size = 5) +
    scale_colour_brewer(palette = 'Set1', direction = 1, name="") +
  geom_line(#Then Leeds and Bradford
    data =  prod.data %>% filter(Region_name %in% c('Leeds','Bradford'), highlow == 'high'),
    aes(x = DATE, y = job_output_propofUKtotal_movingav, group = Region_name, colour = Region_name),
    alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
    scale_colour_brewer(palette = 'Set1', direction = 1, name="") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16,18), name="") +
  xlab('year') +
  facet_wrap(~SIC07_description_shortened, nrow = 1, labeller = labeller(groupwrap = label_wrap_gen(10)))

p2 <- ggplot() +
  geom_jitter(#Rest of UK first
    data =  prod.data %>% filter(highlow == 'low'),
    aes(x = DATE, y = job_output_propofUKtotal_movingav, group = Region_name),
    alpha = 0.3, size = 1, 
    width = 0.1) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0,0.0000002)) +
  geom_point(#Then Leeds and Bradford
    data =  prod.data %>% filter(Region_name %in% c('Leeds','Bradford'), highlow == 'low'),
    aes(x = DATE, y = job_output_propofUKtotal_movingav, group = Region_name, colour = Region_name, shape = Region_name),
    alpha = 1, size = 5) +
    scale_colour_brewer(palette = 'Set1', direction = 1, name="") +
  geom_line(#Then Leeds and Bradford
    data =  prod.data %>% filter(Region_name %in% c('Leeds','Bradford'), highlow == 'low'),
    aes(x = DATE, y = job_output_propofUKtotal_movingav, group = Region_name, colour = Region_name),
    alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
    scale_colour_brewer(palette = 'Set1', direction = 1, name="") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16,18), name="") +
  xlab('year') +
  facet_wrap(~SIC07_description_shortened, nrow = 1, labeller = labeller(groupwrap = label_wrap_gen(10)))


  

p1 / p2
```
